answer: Age-gated quorum weight resists sybils: an identity's weight in any quorum is capped by a function of its tenure, rising slowly from zero, so a fresh swarm holds almost no decisive power however numerous. A cipher of day-one fakes sits at the base of the ridge with marble-light weight; only identities that have aged through many honest epochs carry real quorum influence. An attacker must pre-age each fake for a long stretch before it matters, turning mass registration into a slow, exposed, individually-maintained investment.
